Lessons.Title: Sequences and their Notations
ExplanationParagraphs: A sequence is an ordered list a1,a2,... indexed by positive integers.
An explicit rule evaluates a_n directly from n; recursive rule uses previous terms and initial condition.
Piecewise sequences depend on index parity or an interval.
Independent Cool-down: calculate a representative source-family example and check the result with the definition.

KeyConcepts.Title: Core definition
KeyConcepts.Definition: A sequence is an ordered list a1,a2,... indexed by positive integers.
KeyConcepts.Rule: An explicit rule evaluates a_n directly from n; recursive rule uses previous terms and initial condition.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confuse index, count, order or probability assumptions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Leads to incorrect exponent, multiplicity or denominator.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Identify model and count conditions before computing.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Accepting an answer without validating the original problem conditions.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An algebraic candidate can violate a given domain, interval, sign, model assumption or unit restriction.
